editionLabel: Snowdale Design English original game, ©2021, rules file 6.0
firstPlayerRule: Whoever woke earliest today starts. For consecutive games, one of the previous game's losers starts the next game.
clarifications: Turns proceed clockwise, with an action phase followed by cleanup.
The consecutive-game instruction does not specify how to choose between multiple losing players.
This answer covers the original game's regular rules. Tournament rules and the later anniversary edition are separate.
houseFallback: If the starting criterion is tied or unclear, agree to choose randomly among the eligible players. This is this site's suggested house rule.

PDF spreads and printed page numbers were visually checked; copyright is 2021, despite the 2022 download directory. The original game's identity 176165 appears in the credits.
uncertainty: No initial tie-break or selection between multiple previous losers is specified.
poolReason: The complete rule includes a previous-game-dependent branch; retain it in the catalog rather than trimming it to fit the random mix.

editionLabel: Snowdale Design English campaign opening rules, ©2018, file 1.1 short
firstPlayerRule: Whoever most recently avoided a conflict starts. The campaign rules also allow choosing the starter randomly.
clarifications: Give that person the starting-player token. They begin the adventurer phase, with turns continuing clockwise.
When another round begins, pass the token to the right: the preceding round's last player starts next.
This answer covers the campaign's basic opening rules in the publisher's eleven-page excerpt. Follow additional scenario instructions; the separate Skirmish mode is not covered.
location: Campaign setup step 12; Round overview; Adventurer phase; Status phase; credits

The publisher FAQ/errata at https://snowdaledesign.fi/dawn-of-peacemakers-faq/ was also read on 2026-09-23; its listed corrections do not replace these opening rules. Cached FAQ: dawn-faq.html.
uncertainty: The personal-history criterion has no separate tie-break; random selection is an official alternative.
poolReason: A portable opening-player criterion with an explicitly authorized random alternative. No detailed account of a conflict is needed; the interface also allows skipping.

editionLabel: Steve Jackson Games English base rules, version 1.0, March 2010
firstPlayerRule: The previous game's winner starts, or choose whoever delivers the most expressive cry of “Braaaaains!”.
clarifications: These are alternative starting criteria; the manual does not present the vocal performance as a tie-break after a tied win.
The extra round for tied leaders resolves the end of the game. It is not an initial-start tie-break.
This answer covers the base game's version 1.0 rules.
houseFallback: If neither option settles the choice, or your group prefers another approach, agree to choose randomly. This is this site's suggested house rule.

editionLabel: Steve Jackson Games English rules, version 1.0, January 2013
firstPlayerRule: The previous game's winner starts, or choose whoever makes the best dinosaur sound.
clarifications: Play passes to the left. Remember the starter so everyone receives the same number of turns when the final round is completed.
The dinosaur-sound option is an alternative starting criterion, not a stated tie-break for a previous win.
The extra round between tied leaders decides the winner at the end, not who starts the game.
houseFallback: If neither option settles the choice, or your group prefers another approach, agree to choose randomly. This is this site's suggested house rule.

editionLabel: Steve Jackson Games English rules, version 1.0, July 2009
firstPlayerRule: Whoever has the next upcoming birthday goes first.
clarifications: Setup describes the player's zodiac sign, then explicitly explains the choice in terms of whose birthday comes next.
Play continues clockwise after the opening turn.
houseFallback: If the next birthday is shared or unclear, agree to choose randomly among the tied players. This is this site's suggested house rule.
